proposal.author: Rauan Meiramuly

design.notes: Candidate values are design priors, not selected defaults. Pilot coverage and the selection objective must be committed before running the proposed scorer; evaluation scoring waits for a frozen selected configuration.

ablation.interpretation: The selected Mstar configuration is reported separately if it differs from the fully enabled stage. No new parameter search occurs for ablations.
ablation.parameters: Use the selected candidate's numerical parameters unchanged, including canonical values for inactive components

notes: The fixed Sendros mix always has two zero, two noise and one stale identity. Its fraction labels therefore do not create distinct attack populations.
Attack-free fraction labels also share the same training setup and zero actual attackers. Repeated labels are not independent statistical samples.
Every candidate uses identical cached pilot update matrices. No candidate changes the training aggregator.
Disabled components use canonical placeholder values and do not produce duplicate candidates. The component-free candidate means reference-only; the reference is always leave-one-out.
Undefined attacker allocation when nothing is minted incurs unit cost rather than being dropped. Empty rounds and all honest costs are reported separately.
Commit this plan and the scorer before empirical pilot scoring. Commit the selected parameters and corpus digest before evaluation scoring.
pilot_plan.purpose: Select reward parameters only from disjoint pilot training runs

selection.objective: mean attacker share over attack-present cells plus mean honest false-penalty rate over all cells

design.selection: minimize mean attacker share plus mean honest false-penalty rate; ties prefer fewer components, lower threshold, longer patience, lower EMA decay
design.status: proposed; no pilot selection or evaluation scoring performed

proposal.gap: Existing blockchain reward and penalty systems do not establish whether removing a client's own update from its reward reference reduces the self-inclusion payment to noise free-riders under a controlled comparison that also measures honest-client costs.
proposal.planned_caption: Attacker reward share and honest false-penalty rate under a fixed training trajectory. Each rule scores the same sampled updates. Points summarize evaluation seeds and bars show bootstrap confidence intervals over seeds. Panels separate attack types and registered attacker fractions; the long-run mix is shown separately. Component ablations identify the incremental effect of the client-excluding reference, reputation, and slash/vesting. Lower attacker share alone is insufficient if honest penalties rise. This is a planned caption; no mitigation result is asserted.
proposal.question: Can client-excluding references, reputation and delayed stake penalties reduce attacker rewards while preserving useful participation by honest clients?

references.data: MNIST with heterogeneous clients, free-riders and local contract execution.
references.finding: Reports increasing noise rewards during convergence and higher adversary capture under its threshold allocation.
references.method: Compares public cosine quality with a threshold-gated reward contract and analyzes noise self-inclusion.
references.missing: Does not test its proposed excluding-reference, history and slashing mitigations against poisoning or honest DP noise; uses a verifier stub.
references.problem: Quality disclosure and threshold proofs create different reward incentives.
references.read: Supplied PDF in full; equations and result tables visually checked.
references.title: Tokenized Reward Systems for Federated Learning: The Privacy vs. Fairness Tradeoff
references.use: Reproduction target and motivating failure mechanism. Published figures are comparison data, not our results.

references.data: Private-chain gas experiments across model-parameter sizes; no measured incentive-fairness experiment in the reported evaluation.
references.finding: On-chain model computation becomes costly as dimension grows; the paper explicitly leaves incentive effectiveness unevaluated.
references.method: On-chain sample-weighted alignment scores, off-chain cumulative fairness checks and consistency multipliers.
references.missing: No controlled test of self-inclusion bias against the free-rider/poisoning suite or privacy-noise penalty comparison.
references.problem: Coordinate FL and incentivize contributions with blockchain transparency and scalable computation.
references.read: Abstract, architecture, alignment/fairness/consistency formulas, gas evaluation and limitations opened in full-text author HTML. Official arXiv BibTeX export retrieved.
references.title: Blockchain-based Framework for Scalable and Incentivized Federated Learning
references.use: Closest alignment-and-gas predecessor. Our proposed contribution is the client-excluding reference and controlled common-update evaluation with exact settlement, not the introduction of blockchain rewards or slashing.
references.venue: arXiv:2502.14170; matching WWW Companion publication metadata verified in author HTML and DBLP

references.authors: Dong, Wang, Sun, Kampffmeyer, Knottenbelt, and Xing
references.data: Loan-default prediction on Lending Club, with label-poisoning proposers and malicious voters in a private-chain simulation.
references.finding: Reported experiments preserve useful training and penalize malicious behavior under the stated voting assumptions.
references.method: Peer voting decides whether to accept a model; smart contracts redistribute proposer and voter stakes and exclude bankrupt clients.
references.missing: Does not isolate the direct self-inclusion term in a cosine token scorer or compare the proposed client-excluding rule on identical updates.
references.problem: Central aggregation and malicious clients threaten federated model quality.
references.read: Author full-text abstract, proposal/voting and asset-redistribution algorithms, experimental setup and results opened; journal metadata verified. Publisher-deposited Crossref BibTeX retrieved after DBLP export was unavailable.
references.title: Defending Against Poisoning Attacks in Federated Learning With Blockchain
references.use: Prior reward-and-slash defense. Our work tests a particular scoring correction and honest-client costs, rather than claiming slashing itself as novel.
references.venue: IEEE Transactions on Artificial Intelligence, 5(7):3743--3756; publisher DOI and DBLP metadata checked

subquestions: How does self-inclusion affect noise rewards as training converges, and how closely does the published free-rider effect reproduce?
Which reference, reputation and penalty components change the tradeoff between attacker rewards and honest false penalties under free-riding and poisoning?
How does that tradeoff change for privacy-noised honest updates and published similarity-based rules, and what does exact on-chain settlement cost?
proposal.title: Tokenized incentives for federated learning

published.citation: Sendros, Pavlidis, Perifanis, and Efraimidis. Tokenized Reward Systems for Federated Learning: The Privacy vs. Fairness Tradeoff. arXiv:2611.16065v1, 2026.
notes: Table 3 caption claims residual below three percent for every listed measurement; rounded row values and match percentages are not fully consistent with that caption.
The table labels a ratio of standard deviations as a variance multiplier. Reproduction will distinguish these quantities.

Equation 1 at equal unit stakes and zero quality for absent clients dilutes total payout by the registered count; the adjacent prose instead says pool/K. The constant factor cancels in within-run attacker share when N and K remain fixed.
published.provenance: Transcribed from the supplied source PDF, read in full; equations and result tables also visually inspected. These are published comparison values, not measurements by this repository.

stale_sensitivity.semantics: Latest own reported delta from a round at or before t-lag; zero if none. Persistent stale identities have no honest warm-up, so every stale report is zero.
